estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Citrulline was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (odds ratio (OR<sub>1SD</sub>) = 0.73; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.62-0.86; p <sub>trend</sub> = 0.0002) in the first 5 years of follow-up after taking multiple testing into account, but not after longer follow-up; results for other metabolites did not vary by time to diagnosis.
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate concerns prostate cancer overall during the first five years after blood collection, not an advanced or otherwise aggressive endpoint.

exposures.supporting_excerpt: We aimed to investigate the prospective association between plasma metabolite concentrations and risk of prostate cancer overall, and by time to diagnosis and tumour characteristics, and risk of death from prostate cancer. Seven metabolite concentrations, i.e. acylcarnitine C18:1, amino acids citrulline and trans-4-hydroxyproline, glycerophospholipids PC aa C28:1, PC ae C30:0 and PC ae C30:2, and sphingolipid SM (OH) C14:1, were associated with prostate cancer (p < 0.05), but none of the associations were statistically significant after controlling for multiple testing. After controlling for multiple testing, 12 glycerophospholipids were inversely associated with advanced stage disease, with risk reduction up to 46% per standard deviation increase in concentration (OR<sub>1SD</sub> = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40-0.72; p <sub>trend</sub> = 0.00004 for PC aa C40:3).
exposures.reason: Citrulline was explicitly among the metabolites studied, and the stated metabolite analysis included risk by tumour characteristics, with advanced stage disease reported as the severe incident endpoint. The abstract does not report citrulline's advanced-stage effect, so coverage is qualitative only.
